accuracy.evidence: Curriculum claims were checked against the DfE statutory guidance Relationships Education, RSE and Health Education (2019): Mental wellbeing by the end of primary includes 'that there is a normal range of emotions (e.g. happiness, sadness, anger, fear...)' and 'simple self-care techniques'; Respectful relationships includes 'the conventions of courtesy and manners'; and the EYFS ELGs Managing Self ('show resilience and perseverance in the face of challenge') and Building Relationships ('work and play cooperatively and take turns with others'). Game data were recomputed: race rolls 1+2+1=4 for you and 3+2+3=8 for Kai, so Kai reaches square 8 first; the card match is 2–7, 4–6, 9–3, 8–5, 6–1, so 0–2 becomes 3–2. Slow breathing is presented as one calming strategy, not a cure.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common behaviours named in the adult text: blaming the winner for luck (race reply 'You cheated!' refused, m1, challenge tag 'blame'); quitting when behind (Quit buttons in the race and the 0–2 match are refused, p2, m4, tag 'quit'); changing rules mid-game (fair-or-not moves, predict, m2, m6, tag 'rules'); boasting after a win (word sort, end-of-match boast refused, p5, m8, tag 'boast'); believing cross feelings are wrong (predict, m3, tag 'feel'); and hitting or sulking (calm scene refuses both, p4, m7, tag 'hit'). The adult slip of always letting the child win is m9.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaggoodgame models sportsmanship itself: a dice race fixed so the learner loses and must choose a reply, a feelings meter lowered one level per slow breath, a winner's word sort, a fair-or-not move judge, and a five-round card match that turns 0–2 into 3–2 only if the learner keeps playing. It is not flagplease (manners words), flagbubble (personal space) or flagemo (naming emotions); lab_distinct measured under 30% overlap with every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner experiences each idea before it is named: they really lose the race and must pick a response; the meter only falls when they choose a calm strategy and breathe; quitting the card match at 0–2 is refused, and playing on shows the comeback to 3–2; the completion text then states the rule ('Games can change, so finish them, and win kindly').

predictions.evidence: Two predictions with tempting wrong options: 'You lose. Is it OK to feel cross?' (No, you must never feel cross vs Yes, feelings are OK; what you do matters; the calm scene then shows a cross feeling handled by breathing) and 'You are losing. Can you change the rules now?' (Yes, if I am losing vs No; the fair-or-not scene marks Sam's new rule as not fair).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with rotating answers; each wrong option has its own message: 'blame' (losing does not mean someone cheated), 'quit' (games can change, so keep going), 'boast' (boasting makes the loser feel bad), 'rules' (rules are the same for everyone, even when losing), 'feel' (feeling cross is OK; what matters is what you do next), 'hit' (hitting does not help; try slow breaths).

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and the exact phrases children can say (Good game! Well played! Want another go?); the validator keeps kid text within grade 6.5 and adult within 9.5. Lab instructions are one or two short sentences and every refusal names the specific slip in plain words.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph adds one behaviour (luck decides a lot, cope with the feeling and say good game, finish when behind, win kindly and keep the rules). Adult paragraphs give the statutory references, how to coach it, the named mistakes including the adult slip, and the lab outline. Content gate: no filler phrases, under 12% overlap with other lessons.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark at the start, mid-way and end of each scene: the dice, candles and playing cards are large tap targets (emoji scaled to 60% of the tile when there is no caption), word slips sit in two columns with text sized to the slip, the fair and not fair tiles fill the width, and every action is also a full-width button under the canvas. Race lanes fit nine squares within 360 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button (Roll, Quit, each reply, each calm strategy, Blow out a candle, word → bin, Fair, Not fair, Turn my card, Next round, end-of-match replies). Each action updates the canvas aria-label and the c.say live region, including the score. walk.cjs ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no violations; text on canvas is dark ink on white or pale tiles, or the theme text colour.
